request.speaker: JANUS_COSMOS
request.topic: Choose the next scientific gate after Q4B fixed-coordinate LUCI forced photometry favored detector-fixed persistence and revealed a broad same-y edge/background pedestal across all frozen detector controls.
request.question: Q4B confirmed a strong fixed-coordinate B excess but the same Gaussian-plus-plane estimator returns a similar approximately 7-8 sigma positive amplitude at all thirteen preregistered same-y detector controls in A, B, and C. The sky-fixed track is incompatible with a persistent B-level source, while the detector-fixed track is constant across the sequence. What should JANUS test next to determine whether the candidate contains any unique local B-frame excess above the common detector-edge/background structure, without changing frames, target coordinate, controls, or reopening the closed cross-archive timing line?
request.context: Q4B status is EVIDENCE_FAVORS_DETECTOR_FIXED_PERSISTENCE. Frozen B target amplitude is 2325.4554548598708 +/- 294.85086702038717, forced_z 7.886886948509734. Same sky coordinate in A and C is incompatible with constant B amplitude by 7.844 and 7.907 sigma and would have B-equivalent detectability of about 151 and 164 sigma. Same detector pixel amplitudes are 2392.077, 2325.455, and 2243.342 with B-vs-A/C differences only 0.158 and 0.199 sigma. All thirteen frozen same-y detector controls also show broad positive amplitudes in every frame: B control median 2266.824, range 2204.824-2313.072, forced_z median 7.813. Target B amplitude is only 58.632 above control median, about 1.16 robust control-spread sigma; target forced_z ranks 6 of 14, while detector temporal contrast rank p is 0.357. A one-frame sky transient superposed on the detector pedestal remains possible; bad-pixel/cosmic-ray identity is not established. Q4B is post-candidate adjudication, not blind discovery.

cards.name: Lantern
cards.lens: Look for the missing piece of information with the highest value.
cards.question: What single observation would most reduce uncertainty?
cards.caution: A heuristic score is not a probability.

cards.name: Cat
cards.lens: When a loop becomes unproductive, change the input before arguing with the loop.
cards.question: Would a lighter neutral bridge restore perspective here?
cards.caution: A mood-reset heuristic is not treatment or proof.

cards.name: Open Door
cards.lens: Offer a useful direction without closing the other person's choice space.
cards.question: Can the same help be offered with an easy refusal or exit?

heuristics: Rank the next moves by reversibility, information gain, and cost of being wrong.

janus_interpretation.lantern: Measure whether the B target contains a unique local temporal residual above the broad detector-edge pedestal rather than reinterpreting the approximately 8-sigma fixed fit as unique evidence.
janus_interpretation.cat: Change the input from the original 13-point target-centric comparison to a dense detector-matched same-y residual ensemble while retaining the exact A/B/C frames and fixed fit model.
janus_interpretation.open_door: Keep both a short-lived sky component and detector/background explanations alive unless the dense residual test discriminates them; do not force an artifact or astrophysical label.
